name: Google / Verizon -> NTT OCN route leak
notes: Google (AS15169) accidentally leaked ~160k prefixes to Verizon (AS701), which propagated them globally; the worst-hit network was NTT OCN (AS4713). 25,658 distinct NTT OCN prefixes observed transiting Google -> Verizon at RRC00 in the data fetched on 2026-05-10 (filter='path "_15169_4713"'). Onset 03:22:54 UTC matches the BGPmon-reported 03:22 UTC onset to the minute. Standard route_leak detector (valley-free against the CAIDA serial-2 2017-08 snapshot) does NOT fire on these paths: the canonical leak path '3333 1103 286 701 15169 4713' has directions [c2p, c2p, c2p, p2c, unknown] -- a single p2c (Verizon->Google) is valid valley-free shape, and the 15169->4713 step is 'unknown' because CAIDA doesn't have that pair in its inferred relationships. Detecting this case at the path level requires either a customer-cone-aware detector ('AS15169 is not authorized to transit for AS4713') or more comprehensive AS-relationship data than the public CAIDA snapshot provides. This is an open detector gap rather than a missed signal; the data shows the leak clearly.
